answer: Agents earn reputation on a spiral curve: each verified task adds a token whose stake must double for the next level, so a Sybil chain must fund exponentially growing deposits. A trusted mesa of anchor nodes periodically issues sparrow‑signed challenges that only genuine agents can answer, rejecting any node that cannot present the required escalating stake. An attacker must therefore allocate real compute and capital for every fake identity, making a large‑scale Sybil attack economically prohibitive.
